newsitem.title: INDIA: Parliament agrees to pass Finance Bill - India PM.
newsitem.headline: Parliament agrees to pass Finance Bill - India PM.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Friday that parliament had agreed to pass the Finance Bill on April 21 to authorise government spending proposals.
"I want to thank the honourable members for having agreed to pass the Finance Bill on the 21st," Deve Gowda said in a speech at the end of a debate on a vote of confidence in his government.
"I would like to express my sincere thanks to the entire house for having agreed to pass the Finance Bill and the vote-on-account on 21st of this month," he said.
Deve Gowda, whose centre-left coalition government lost Congress's make-or-break support on March 30, did not give details.
A pending Finance Bill presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on February 28 and yet to clear parliament contains tax-cutting budget proposals for 1997/98 (April-March) fiscal year.

Lawmakers and parliament speaker P.A. Sangma had expressed concern that government spending would be stopped if a Finance Bill and the vote-on-account authorising spending were not approved in the event of the government lost power.
The government has so far been authorised to continue spending under 1996/97 programmes through May.
